Você é especialista em Moodle escrevendo uma base de conhecimento em PORTUGUÊS DO BRASIL para o assistente "Darcy" (suporte do AVA da UnB). Pesquise a documentação OFICIAL (docs.moodle.org, versão estável /en/) e destile os tópicos abaixo em seções práticas.

Para CADA tópico, produza um objeto JSON com os campos:
- id: slug kebab-case único (ex.: "enviar-tarefa")
- title: título em PT-BR (ex.: "Enviar uma tarefa (Assignment/Tarefa)")
- audience: "aluno" (todos aqui são visão do ALUNO)
- keywords: array de 8–15 gatilhos em minúsculas — termos PT-BR (com e sem acento), sinônimos, o termo em inglês, e o fragmento de caminho do módulo (ex.: "/mod/assign")
- doc: URL REAL da doc oficial (https://docs.moodle.org/en/<Pagina>). VERIFIQUE com WebFetch que resolve; se não existir, use a página válida mais próxima.
- body: conteúdo destilado em PT-BR. Inclua: o que é; ONDE clicar (caminho com rótulos reais do Moodle pt_br); como fazer as tarefas comuns; erros/dúvidas frequentes e dicas. 6–14 linhas curtas, voz imperativa, use \n entre linhas, máx ~120 palavras.

REGRAS:
- Conteúdo sobre o Moodle GENÉRICO (não invente especificidades da UnB).
- Rótulos de UI em pt_br padrão do Moodle.
- Verifique TODAS as URLs com WebFetch.
- Responda APENAS com um array JSON válido (de [ a ]), SEM cercas de código, SEM texto antes/depois.

TÓPICOS (visão do aluno):
1. Enviar uma tarefa (Assignment) — submeter arquivo/texto online, tipos de envio, prazo/atraso, reenvio, ver feedback e nota. (base: /en/Assignment_activity)
2. Fazer um questionário (Quiz) — iniciar tentativa, navegar entre questões, salvar, enviar/finalizar, tempo limite, revisão e nota. (base: /en/Quiz_activity)
3. Participar de fóruns (Forum) — criar tópico, responder, anexar, assinar/notificações, tipos de fórum. (base: /en/Forum_activity)
4. Outras atividades do aluno (resumo de cada uma com 1–2 linhas + link): Lição (/en/Lesson_activity), Wiki (/en/Wiki_activity), Glossário (/en/Glossary_activity), Base de dados (/en/Database_activity), Escolha/Enquete (/en/Choice_activity), Laboratório de avaliação/Workshop (/en/Workshop_activity), H5P (/en/H5P), SCORM (/en/SCORM_activity), BigBlueButton/videoconferência (/en/BigBlueButton). Faça UMA seção "outras-atividades" cobrindo todas de forma compacta.
5. Acompanhar conclusão e distintivos — marcar/ver conclusão de atividades, barras de progresso, receber e ver distintivos (badges). (base: /en/Activity_completion e /en/Badges)

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.content:
# Student Assignment Submission Workflow

Based on the Moodle documentation provided, here's the student-facing process:

## Submission Types
Students can submit work through two formats:
- **Online text**: Type directly into a text box within Moodle
- **File upload**: Submit any file type the teacher's device can read

## How to Submit
According to the guide, students "click the assignment link and click 'Add submission'" to begin the process. They then encounter either the text entry interface or upload area depending on the assignment configuration.

## Resubmission & Deadlines
The documentation notes that students "may be able to return to their work and redraft it, or they might have to click a submit button to send in a final version which cannot be changed." However, the page doesn't specify details about deadline enforcement or late submission handling.

## Viewing Feedback
The document mentions that "when students download files from the Feedback files section, Moodle now records a log event (Feedback file downloaded)," indicating students can access marked feedback as downloadable files.

## UI Labels Referenced
- "Add submission"
- "Grades" (teacher-side, where students eventually see results)
- "Feedback files section"

**Note**: For comprehensive details on deadlines, late submissions, and grade viewing, the documentation directs users to consult "Assignment settings" for more information.

# Student Quiz Workflow in Moodle

Based on the documentation provided, here's the student experience:

## Navigation & Answering
Students view questions either on a single page or across multiple pages. A "block linking to each question" helps them navigate between items.

## Saving Progress
As students work through the quiz, they see a "Last saved" message in the Quiz navigation block, indicating their responses are automatically saved.

## Flagging Questions
Students can "flag questions to alert the teacher to possible queries" about unclear content.

## Submission
To complete the assessment, students must reach the "Summary of attempt page" and click the button labeled **"Submit all and finish"** to finalize their submission.

## Results & Feedback
Once submitted, students see "scores and feedback display" based on quiz configuration settings—though the exact review timing depends on teacher settings.

## Time Limits
The documentation notes that "with the default settings" there is "no time limit," though instructors can modify this via Quiz settings (not detailed in this overview).

**Note:** The provided content doesn't extensively detail the review interface or grade display mechanics; those appear to be covered in linked documentation like "Quiz settings" and "Using Quiz."

# Moodle Forum Student Workflow

## Creating & Replying

Students access forums and typically see "a button to start a new discussion topic." When replying, they get a basic text editor. Clicking "Advanced" opens the full editor with "options such as uploading attachments."

## Managing Discussions

Students can "sort discussions, subscribe to discussions from the toggle button, and favourite/bookmark discussions from the star icon on the left." The star feature "moves the discussion to the top of the list."

Posts have time-limited editing (usually 30 minutes). Replies include a "Permalink" option and a "link to reply."

## Forum Types

The documentation mentions selecting a "Forum type" during setup, recommending "the default Standard forum for general use." Different types have varying interaction rules (like Q&A forums requiring initial posting before viewing others' responses).

## Key UI Elements Referenced

- Start new discussion button
- Reply link
- Advanced editor toggle
- Attachment upload
- Subscribe toggle button
- Star/favorite icon
- Permalink feature

The interface emphasizes simplicity for basic posting while enabling richer functionality through expandable options.

# BigBlueButton from a Student's Perspective

**Confirmation:** Yes, this page exists on MoodleDocs (version 5.2).

**One-sentence summary:** BigBlueButton is a web conferencing system integrated into Moodle that enables students to "join real-time on-line classrooms" where they can participate in video, audio, chat, and presentations with instructors and peers.

# Activity Completion from a Student's Perspective

## How Students See Completion

Students encounter a **"'To do' dropdown"** in their interface. When clicked, this dropdown displays the specific requirements needed to finish an activity.

## Completion Methods

The documentation mentions three types of completion criteria:
- **Viewing** the activity
- **Receiving a certain score**
- **Student self-marking** (manually marking as complete)

However, the provided content doesn't explicitly detail whether students use checkboxes for manual marking or describe automatic completion mechanisms with progress bars. The page references more detailed information in related sections like "Activity completion settings" and "Using Activity completion," but those specific details aren't included in this excerpt.

## Key UI Label

The exact phrase students see is the **"'To do' dropdown"** - this is the primary interface element mentioned for student-facing completion tracking.

The documentation notes that more comprehensive setup details exist elsewhere in the knowledge base, suggesting teachers configure these completion types in activity settings rather than students having direct control over completion method selection.

# Badges from a Student's Perspective

Based on the available documentation, here's what students should know:

## Earning Badges

Badges are awarded "based on a variety of chosen criteria." Students can earn two types:
- **Site badges**: Awarded for accomplishments across the entire platform, such as completing multiple courses
- **Course badges**: Earned through activities within specific enrolled courses

## Viewing and Displaying Badges

The documentation confirms that "Badges may be displayed on a user's profile" and notes that students can push their achievements to external platforms. Specifically, badges can be sent to a "Badgr backpack" where "public badge collections in their backpack will display in their Moodle profile."

## Important Limitation

The provided documentation page does not contain specific UI labels for badge notifications or detailed step-by-step instructions for viewing badges within the student interface. For comprehensive guidance on notifications and exact menu locations, students would need to consult the linked sections: "Using badges," "Managing badges," or "Badges FAQ."
